Definition: from G3844 and the middle voice of a derivative of G3454; to relate near, i.e. (by implication) encourage, console:--comfort.
BiblicalUsage: Paramytheomai means to comfort, to console, to speak gently to. Many of the Jews come to Martha and Mary to comfort them concerning their brother Lazarus, and Paul tells the church to comfort the feebleminded, support the weak, be patient toward all men.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe comfort is a ministry of presence: the Jews sit with the sisters, and the church is told to comfort the feebleminded — not to fix them, but to stay with them.
